messages:
infra-alerts-bot: :rotating_light: [ALERT] node-23: repeated NV driver resets detected (Xid codes: 13, 79). ECC counters rising. Canary eviction of pods on node-23 initiated at 2127604320. Auto-restart attempted (3/3) and failed. Logs: https://internal.logs/redwood/node-23

Sophie: looking. saw a small spike in OOM kills on the runtime pods ~2127604305, then driver reset. nodes show GPU going offline/online quickly.

Deepak: @Sophie thanks. can you confirm if dedicated workloads were on node-23? any customer-facing routes hit?

Sophie: quick check - two dedicated pools had ephemeral pods there (dedicated-gpu-a and batch-gpu-c). Traffic rerouted by routing service; we saw increased 5xx from a couple customers for ~40s before fallback. Not a full outage.

Mike: I'm oncall infra. I've pulled dmesg and nvidia-smi logs, attaching snippet:

```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1234.568012] nvidia: probe of 0000:65:00.0 failed with error -5
[ 1234.568123] NVRM: Xid (13:0000): GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1234.569000] EDAC MC1: ECC error detected in DRAM, syndrome=0x4a
```

Mike: looks like repeated driver resets + ECC page reports. Could be hardware degradation or thermal/PSU issue. Node metric: GPU temp peaked at 92C before resets.

Jessie: @Mike if temp hit 92C that's concerning. What's current node state? is it cordoned?

Mike: cordoned at 2127604360 and pods evicted. kube drain executed with --delete-local-data --ignore-daemonsets. Command:

```
kubectl cordon node-23
kubectl drain node-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

Sophie: routing team confirmed no active canaries on customer-sensitive routes remain on node-23. Support lead, any impacted customers to notify?

Support Lead: Support noticed transient errors for Customer A and Customer C (embedding requests returned 500 for ~30–45s). No SLA breach expected given automatic retries. I'll open a brief incident note and ping the account teams.

Deepak: Next steps: 1) Validate whether this is a single-GPU failure vs host-level power/thermal. 2) If hardware, schedule cordon + replace. 3) If driver/software, attempt staged driver reload on a non-prod host to reproduce.

Sophie: repro attempt on a staging node (staging-gpu-7) with same model load failed to produce resets after 15m. That leans hardware.

Mike: I'll attempt a controlled driver rebind on node-23 to see if we can get a clean kernel recovery once workload drained. Steps:

```
# on host
systemctl stop runc-containerd.service
modprobe -r nvidia_uvm nvidia_drm nvidia
modprobe nvidia
systemctl start runc-containerd.service
```

Mike: doing modprobe -r now, will only proceed if infra tooling snapshot done.

infra-alerts-bot: snapshot created: /snapshots/node-23-2127604365.tar.gz

Mike: modprobe removed, modules reloaded. nvidia-smi still shows driver inconsistency; system logs show new parity ECC reports. I'm escalating for hardware RMA.

Jessie: please add node-23 to quarantine pool and mark as RMA candidate. Also check adjacent rack power rails and BMC logs.

Sophie: confirmed adjacent nodes in same rack show elevated PCIe errors but not resets. Could be shared PSU or switch. Opening infra ticket: INFRA-7290.

Support Lead: I'll send a proactive note to affected customers summarizing: short blip impacting a small subset of GPU-backed requests; automatic routing mitigated broader impact; we're investigating root cause and will follow up.

Deepak: good. For rollback/fallback: enable permanent fallback policy for heavy inference routes until node-23 is replaced. Set routing weight to avoid nodes in that rack.

Sophie: applying routing exclusion now (tools: rwt set-exclude --rack rack-7).

Sophie: exclusion applied at 2127604480. Monitor for any increase in latency elsewhere.

Mike: hardware team has acknowledged INFRA-7290 and scheduled on-site for RMA at 2127608000 (ETA ~1.0h). I'll keep node cordoned until replaced.

Jessie: once RMA done, we'll run burn-in tests (48h low-latency stream + ECC stress) before returning to production pool.

Support Lead: noted. I'll update incident note and include timeline and mitigation steps.

Sophie: summary for post-incident: cause suspected hardware-level ECC/parity leading to NV driver resets + transient OOMs on runtime; immediate mitigations: cordon & drain node-23, routing exclusion for rack-7, driver reload attempt (failed), hardware RMA scheduled. Customer impact: brief 500s for limited customers, no SLA breach expected. Follow-ups: INFRA-7290, RMA + burn-in, postmortem with telemetry (dmesg, ECC counters, GPU temp history).

Deepak: thanks team. I'll own the postmortem and tag with severity P2 if hardware confirmed. Assigning to Deepak/Mike/Jessie.

oncall-rotation: :thumbsup: closing on-call window, will hand back to infra team.

Sophie: closing thread. I'll post the incident note link when Support Lead adds it. :white_check_mark:
